recommended_title: Reporting Scores After Prompt Search: A Selection-Aware Posterior Interval from a Hierarchical Latent-Difficulty Model
central_question: When a configuration is chosen on a finite benchmark sample and its search-time score is then reported, how large is the optimism of that score, which factors control it, and can a selection-aware interval built only from the search-time evaluation log give a more reliable report of fresh-question accuracy?
central_thesis: The naive best-of-search score with a Wilson interval is biased upward and too narrow when many configurations are compared on few questions; an empirical-Bayes hierarchical logistic latent-difficulty posterior interval, fitted to the full logged (question, config, outcome) triples and agnostic to the searcher, lowers the mean 90%-level interval score relative to naive, Bonferroni-Wilson, and question-resampling reporters in the sealed final evaluation (qualified outcome), but it keeps residual positive bias and sub-nominal coverage in specific real-data regimes (successive halving, large N), so the claim is conditional on the studied worlds.
narrative_rationale: The final evaluation completed with outcome 'qualified' (final.qualification.outcome), mean interval score 0.1449 vs 0.2202 (naive), 0.1974 (Bonferroni), 0.2461 (resample) (final.metric.*), coverage 0.929 and null-control coverage 0.929. This gives a positive but narrow, conditional story. The task asks about the gap between reported and fresh-question accuracy and a more reliable reporting method; the run answers both through evaluator-owned synthetic worlds with exact truth and cached real Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct outcomes on MMLU-Pro under 24 prompt configurations, with exhaustive and successive-halving searchers and null/constant controls. A thesis-first estimator-and-evidence paper beats a campaign-chronology paper: the three model variants evaluated in search are close in score and only the frozen winner has a final evaluation, so they are best presented as a width/coverage trade-off comparison, not as a progression. Per-case results show where the method wins big (synthetic and real exhaustive, small N), where it is merely on par with naive (real halving, large N), and where a simple question-resampling reporter is slightly better (real exhaustive cases) or catastrophically bad (halving) - that heterogeneity is the scientifically interesting content and must be foregrounded for honesty. No downstream_study block exists in paper_data.json, so no downstream-study claims.
edit_framing_decision: Edit mode is not enabled (no previous_paper or edit context staged); there is no prior manuscript to preserve, broaden or recenter, so the story is chosen fresh from grounded results.
staged_input_impact: No staged prior paper or new-program inputs exist; the framing rests only on paper_data.json, task contract, and the winning program source in the investigation directory.

method_groups.name: Naive best-of-search score with Wilson 90% interval
method_groups.include_reason: The status-quo reporting practice the task questions; its signed bias (final.metric.naive_signed_bias = 0.0366) quantifies the optimism gap and the incumbent for scoring.

method_groups.name: Bonferroni-widened Wilson interval and question-resampling (bootstrap-optimism) reporter
method_groups.include_reason: Two evaluator-supplied selection-aware alternatives (final.metric.bonferroni_baseline_score, final.metric.resample_baseline_score); needed so the proposed gain is not against a strawman. Resample is better on some real exhaustive cases and fails under halving.

method_groups.name: Empirical-Bayes hierarchical logistic latent-difficulty posterior interval (frozen selection)
method_groups.include_reason: Winner of search (result.best_correct_score = -0.1480) and the evaluated method in the sealed final run. Logit P = a_config - b_question with EB variance estimates, ignorable-selection argument, Laplace draws plus Gauss-Hermite over fresh difficulties, 5/95% quantiles, calibration factor kappa, degenerate-world guards.

method_groups.name: Search-stage variants: parametric-bootstrap pivot calibration; config-by-subject interaction random effects
method_groups.include_reason: Two scored alternatives to the winner (result.top_program_02, result.top_program_03; 3 of 3 attempts scored, 0 unscored). Shows narrower intervals (c02 width 0.085, coverage 0.77) lose on interval score and extra interaction structure (c03) did not beat the plain model. Search-plane only; report as variant comparison, not as final evidence, and not as a significance ranking (single evaluation each).

method_groups.name: Negative controls (synthetic null N1, real permuted-config null N2, constant-zero world Z1)
method_groups.include_reason: Check the reporter does not manufacture signal and handles degenerate worlds (final.metric.null_control_abs_bias, null_control_coverage, constant_control_error = 0.0).

results_focus: Sealed-final aggregate: mean interval score of the proposed reporter vs naive, Bonferroni and resample reporters (final.metric.*), with spread across the 8 final seeds (final.evidence.episodes). State outcome 'qualified' (final.qualification.outcome) with the completed status and 100% replication completion; do not extend into generality.

Optimism gap and its drivers: naive signed bias per case (large at small N=60 ~0.051, smaller at N=200 ~0.022-0.025, ~0.009 at N=600; synthetic ~0.05-0.07; derived from per-case final episodes) versus the proposed reporter's residual bias; discuss N, K, searcher. Compute exact values from final.evidence.episodes; flag that per-case diagnostics have candidate_diagnostics_trust 'unverified'.

Per-case interval score and coverage (synthetic P1,P2; real exhaustive P3,P5,P6; real halving P4) vs 0.90 nominal: large gains over naive on synthetic and small-N real cases, parity with naive on P4/P6, and sub-nominal coverage on P4 and P6; resample baseline slightly better on some real exhaustive cases and far worse under halving (P2, P4).
Negative controls: null-control coverage 0.929 and absolute bias 0.017 vs naive; constant-zero error 0.0.

Search-stage width-versus-coverage trade-off among three scored model variants (result.top_program_01..03; coverage 0.915 / 0.8925 / 0.77; widths 0.124 / 0.120 / 0.085), kept clearly separate from the final plane.

Does the optimism gap change conclusions? Only supported to the extent that a miscalibrated interval's miss penalty and coverage show reported numbers are unreliable; do not claim ranking-reversal results unless computed from artifacts (none are in paper_data.json).

notes_for_writer: Final outcome is 'qualified' with status 'completed' (final.qualification.outcome/status/correct); state it plainly, but publication eligibility does not equal broad scientific validity: keep claims conditional (one 0.5B model, MMLU-Pro, 24 prompt configs, two searchers: exhaustive and successive halving, evaluator-owned synthetic worlds; no DSPy/MIPRO, no adaptive Ladder-style reporting).

Present the metric as 'mean interval score at 90% level (lower is better)'; the internal combined_score is its negative and must not appear by name. Interval score = width + 20x miss distance; worst-case failed replication IS=20.

No downstream_study block is present: do not describe a downstream study. Keep search-plane (three variants) separate from final-plane (frozen winner only). Per-variant final results do not exist; do not invent them. Search score differences among variants (-0.1480, -0.1519, -0.1562) come from one scored evaluation each and are not a significance ranking.

The final per-case diagnostics are derived from final.evidence.episodes with candidate_diagnostics_trust='unverified'; aggregate metrics in final.metric.* are the authoritative numbers. Compute per-case means and across-seed spread from episode records with a script included in the code package; uncertainty = spread over the 8 final seeds (9101-9108), each with R=30 replications (R=10 for Z1).

Be honest about heterogeneity: proposed reporter is roughly on par with naive on real halving (P4: 0.156 vs 0.161, with larger signed bias 0.031 vs 0.025) and at large N (P6: 0.096 vs 0.096), with coverage below 0.90 on P4 (~0.89) and P6 (~0.83); resample baseline is slightly better on several real exhaustive cases (P3, P5, P6, N2) but very poor under halving (P2 ~0.59, P4 ~0.26). Recompute these from episodes before quoting.

Frame the answer to research question 1 via the naive signed bias (0.0366 aggregate) and its dependence on N, K, world, and searcher; do not claim a decision-reversal effect without a computed artifact. Treat 'does it affect conclusions' as partially addressed through coverage/miss penalty and say what is not tested.

The real-LLM outcome tensor (Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct on MMLU-Pro, 24 configs, pinned revisions) was shipped with the task package and derived by the task authors; this run did not regenerate it. Say so. Do not claim the paper ran its own LLM inference or its own DSPy/MIPRO searches. Report actual compute: final evaluation episodes ~6 s each (from episode duration fields).

Mechanism motivation: selection by searchers uses only observed outcomes, so selection is ignorable for the likelihood, which licenses one code path for both searchers; shrinkage of config effects removes winner's-curse bias; the 5/95% quantiles minimise expected interval score for the predictive distribution. State the ignorability argument as motivation, not as proven in the real-data regime, since 1-D difficulty is misspecified for real multi-dimensional subject-by-config effects (c03 attempted that extension in search and did not beat the plain model).

Related work: use only references in references.bib that are real and relevant (Dwork et al. 2015 adaptive-data-analysis entries; reusable holdout; Feldman/Steinke-style variance work; the Ullman et al. perspective). The bib contains many irrelevant medical/unrelated entries; do not cite them. Starter-literature works (MMLU-Pro, DSPy, MIPRO, Ladder, Inference on Winners, Valid post-selection inference, Sclar et al., Polo et al.) are not in references.bib; cite them only after verified retrieval/addition, otherwise describe the relation without a citation.

Overview figure uses generate-concept-figure (only one concept figure planned). All figures full text width (5.5 in single-column ICLR template); export PDF and 300-DPI PNG; reference the PDF in LaTeX; never upscale rasters.

Body budget 8-9 pages: spend space on problem formalization (selection, truth definition, interval score), the estimator with enough detail to reimplement, the per-case comparison, bias/coverage diagnostics, null controls, and a substantial limitations section (single small LLM, two searchers, evaluator-defined worlds, kappa calibrated on a local development harness using the search split, residual undercoverage, no adaptive reporting). Do not pad with search narrative.
Anonymize: no author names, no self-identifying links or run directory paths; include LLM Usage section (appendix permitted).
Threshold-style rates: if one is used, use 'interval coverage' (fraction of intervals containing the truth) with a single meaning; do not introduce other thresholded labels.
